name: Albiglutide
summary: A withdrawn once-weekly GLP-1 diabetes drug; it was never a weight-loss product and produced modest weight effects in trials.
lead: Albiglutide (brand names Tanzeum in the United States and Eperzan in Europe) is a once-weekly injectable glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist that was approved to improve blood-sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes. It was developed by Human Genome Sciences and marketed by GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) .

name: Peptide YY
summary: A satiety hormone made in the gut; infusion studies show reduced intake, but it is not an approved or established appearance tool.
lead: Peptide YY (PYY) is a 36-amino-acid gut hormone released by L-cells in the ileum and colon after eating. It acts to reduce appetite and slow gastric emptying, and it belongs to the neuropeptide Y family . The main circulating form, PYY(3-36), acts largely through the Y2 receptor .

name: ACE-031
summary: An experimental myostatin-blocking fusion protein tested in healthy women and Duchenne boys; trials ended and it is not approved.
lead: ACE-031 is a soluble fusion protein of the activin receptor type IIB (ActRIIB) and the Fc part of IgG1. It acts as a decoy that binds myostatin and related ligands that limit muscle growth .

name: Stamulumab
summary: A discontinued Wyeth antibody that blocks myostatin; tested in muscular dystrophy, never approved or studied for physique.
lead: Stamulumab (MYO-029) is an experimental monoclonal antibody that binds myostatin, a protein that limits muscle growth. It was developed by Wyeth as a possible treatment for muscular dystrophy .

name: ARO-INHBE
summary: An experimental RNAi drug against INHBE aimed at fat distribution; only early trial registrations exist so far.
lead: ARO-INHBE is an investigational RNA interference (RNAi) therapy aimed at the INHBE gene, which encodes a liver-derived protein involved in fat distribution. It is being tested in people with obesity, with and without type 2 diabetes, and in a planned trial in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). It is not approved for any use anywhere.

name: ARO-ALK7
summary: An experimental RNAi drug against ALK7 for obesity; a single early trial is recruiting and no results exist.
lead: ARO-ALK7 is an investigational RNA interference (RNAi) therapy directed at ALK7, a receptor involved in fat-cell signalling. It is being tested in adults with obesity, with and without type 2 diabetes. It is not approved for any use.

name: WVE-007
summary: An experimental liver-targeted siRNA aimed at cutting visceral fat while sparing muscle; early company data only, not approved.
lead: WVE-007 is an investigational GalNAc-conjugated small interfering RNA (siRNA) developed by Wave Life Sciences for obesity. It is designed to silence INHBE messenger RNA in the liver, lowering circulating Activin E, a liver-secreted protein that is described as restraining fat breakdown in fat cells. The stated goal is preferential loss of visceral fat while preserving lean mass.

name: ALN-6222
summary: An experimental INHBE-targeting RNAi drug that has just entered its first obesity trial; nothing is known about results.
lead: ALN-6222 is an investigational RNA interference (RNAi) therapy that targets INHBE, a gene linked to fat distribution, in people with obesity. It is not approved for any use.

name: Monlunabant
summary: An experimental oral CB1 blocker for weight loss that showed modest results and some neuropsychiatric side effects in Phase 2.
lead: Monlunabant (also INV-202, MRI-1891) is an investigational, peripherally selective cannabinoid receptor 1 (CB1) inverse agonist developed for obesity and metabolic disease. It was discovered by researchers at the US National Institutes of Health and developed by Inversago Pharma, and is now associated with Novo Nordisk. It is not approved for any use.

name: CRB-913
summary: An experimental CB1 blocker that boosted GLP-1 drugs in obese mice; human data are not yet public.
lead: CRB-913 is an investigational peripherally acting cannabinoid receptor 1 (CB1) inverse agonist being studied for obesity. It is not approved for any use.

name: Nimacimab
summary: An experimental anti-CB1 antibody for obesity that is still in Phase 2, with no appearance-use evidence.
lead: Nimacimab is an investigational monoclonal antibody that targets the cannabinoid-1 receptor (CB1) and is being developed for obesity and other metabolic conditions. Unlike earlier small-molecule CB1 blockers, it is designed to act on peripheral tissues rather than the brain, with the aim of avoiding the neuropsychiatric side effects that ended earlier drugs in this class.

name: NAD+ injections
summary: Injected NAD+ is sold as a longevity and energy treatment, but no controlled human trials support it for aging or appearance.
lead: NAD+ injections are parenteral (injected or infused) preparations of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, a coenzyme found in all living cells. They are marketed by some wellness and longevity clinics, and discussed online, as an anti-aging or energy-boosting treatment.

name: Glutathione injections
summary: Injected glutathione is used for skin lightening, but its effectiveness is unclear and the Philippine government advises against IV use.
lead: Glutathione (GSH) is a small tripeptide made of glutamate, cysteine and glycine that cells produce naturally and use as a major antioxidant. Intravenous or intramuscular glutathione is promoted in some countries and online communities as a skin-lightening treatment, often alongside vitamin C.

name: VIP (Vasoactive intestinal peptide)
summary: A natural vasodilating neuropeptide sold as a research peptide, with no human evidence for any appearance use.
lead: Vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) is a 28-amino-acid neuropeptide found in the gut, brain, heart, lungs and other tissues. It acts through the VPAC1 and VPAC2 receptors and has vasodilating, smooth-muscle-relaxing and immune-modulating effects.

name: Aviptadil
summary: Synthetic VIP used for erectile dysfunction and tested in COVID-19 lung failure; no appearance evidence.
lead: Aviptadil is a synthetic form of vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP), a 28-amino-acid neuropeptide first characterised in 1970. It has been used as an injectable in combination with phentolamine for erectile dysfunction in some European countries, and it has been studied as an intravenous or inhaled treatment for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), pulmonary hypertension and COVID-19 respiratory failure.

name: Ara-290
summary: An EPO-derived repair peptide tested in small neuropathy trials, with no data for appearance or recovery in healthy people.
lead: ARA 290, also known as cibinetide, is an 11-amino-acid peptide engineered from the structure of erythropoietin (EPO). It was designed to activate the innate repair receptor involved in tissue protection without raising red blood cell counts, avoiding the thrombosis risk associated with recombinant EPO.

name: B7-33
summary: A lab-made relaxin mimic studied in animals for fibrosis; no human trials and no documented appearance use.
lead: B7-33 is a laboratory-designed, single-chain peptide derived from the B-chain of human relaxin-2, a pleiotropic hormone with vasodilatory and anti-fibrotic properties. It was engineered as a simpler and cheaper mimic of recombinant relaxin-2 (serelaxin), which is costly and laborious to produce .

name: PE-22-28
summary: A spadin-derived peptide studied in rodents as a fast-acting antidepressant; no human data and no appearance use documented.
lead: PE-22-28 is a synthetic seven-residue peptide (Gly-Val-Ser-Trp-Gly-Leu-Arg) derived from spadin, an endogenous peptide fragment of the sortilin propeptide that blocks the TREK-1 potassium channel . It was designed as a shorter, more potent and more stable analogue of spadin for antidepressant research.

name: PNC-27
summary: A p53-derived peptide shown to lyse cancer cells in lab studies; no human trials, sold only as a research chemical.
lead: PNC-27 is a 32-residue chimeric peptide that joins a segment of the p53 tumour-suppressor protein (residues 12-26, the region that binds HDM-2/MDM2) to a membrane-penetrating sequence . In laboratory studies its authors report that it kills cancer cells, but not normal cells, by binding HDM-2 on the cancer-cell membrane and forming pores that lyse the cell .

name: Erythropoietin
summary: A kidney hormone and anaemia drug used for endurance doping; indirect link to appearance, with serious cardiovascular warnings.
lead: Erythropoietin (EPO) is a glycoprotein hormone made mainly by the kidneys in response to low oxygen; it stimulates red blood cell production in the bone marrow. Its gene is switched on by hypoxia-inducible factors, and it signals through the EPO receptor and JAK2 .

name: Abaloparatide
summary: An approved osteoporosis bone-builder that forums speculate about for bonesmashing and lengthening; no appearance trials exist.
lead: Abaloparatide (brand name Tymlos) is a synthetic 34-amino-acid analogue of parathyroid hormone-related protein, PTHrP(1-34), approved in the United States for osteoporosis. Its US label covers postmenopausal women at high fracture risk and men with osteoporosis at high risk, as an injectable bone-forming (anabolic) drug .
claims: Abaloparatide could help rebuild or thicken facial bone alongside bonesmashing and orthodontics.
Taking a PTH analogue during puberty could affect skeletal growth.
It could speed or strengthen bone formation during limb lengthening.

name: Salmon calcitonin
summary: A fish-derived calcitonin used for Paget's disease and hypercalcaemia; it slows bone loss and has no documented appearance use.
lead: Salmon calcitonin is a synthetic form of calcitonin, a 32-amino-acid peptide hormone made by thyroid C cells that lowers blood calcium by inhibiting bone resorption. The salmon version differs from the human sequence at many positions and is reported to be more potent and longer acting .

name: Osteocalcin
summary: A bone-made protein and proposed hormone studied for bone and metabolism; no looks-related use has been tested in humans.
lead: Osteocalcin (gene BGLAP) is a small, 49-amino-acid protein made by bone-forming cells (osteoblasts) and found in bone and dentin. Its synthesis and calcium binding depend on vitamin K-dependent carboxylation, and its blood level is widely used as a marker of bone formation.

name: Irisin
summary: A proposed exercise hormone from muscle; mouse fat-browning findings are intriguing but human evidence is thin and disputed.
lead: Irisin is a protein fragment cleaved from FNDC5 (fibronectin type III domain-containing protein 5) and was proposed in 2012 as a hormone released by muscle during exercise. Boström and colleagues reported in Nature that it was PGC-1-alpha-dependent and drove brown-fat-like changes in white fat tissue in mice.

name: Adropin
summary: A liver and brain peptide linked to fat metabolism in mice; human data are blood-level associations only.
lead: Adropin is a 76-amino-acid peptide encoded by the ENHO gene, reported in 2008 in Cell Metabolism as a secreted factor linking dietary macronutrient intake with energy homeostasis and lipid metabolism in mice. Its name derives from Latin words for 'set fire to' and 'fat'.

name: Asprosin
summary: A fat-derived fasting hormone that raises glucose and appetite in mice; high levels track with obesity but no appearance use exists.
lead: Asprosin is a fasting-induced protein hormone cleaved from fibrillin-1 (encoded by FBN1) and released mainly from white fat. It was described in 2016 by Atul Chopra's group at Baylor College of Medicine as raising blood glucose during fasting, and in 2017 as stimulating appetite through the brain.

name: Obestatin
summary: A ghrelin-gene peptide first reported to curb appetite; both that effect and its receptor remain disputed.
lead: Obestatin is a 23-residue peptide encoded by the same gene as ghrelin. It was reported in Science in 2005 as opposing ghrelin's effects on food intake, and it was found through computer analysis of genome sequences.

name: Limostatin
summary: A fruit-fly hormone that switches insulin down during fasting; studied only in insects, with no human data.
lead: Limostatin (Lst) is a peptide hormone first identified in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster. It is released from gut-associated endocrine cells when nutrients are scarce and suppresses the production and secretion of insulin-like peptides, which made it the first well-characterised example of a "decretin", a fasting-induced hormone that opposes insulin.

name: Alamandine
summary: A blood-pressure-regulating peptide of the renin-angiotensin system; interesting cardiovascular biology in rodents, no human trials.
lead: Alamandine is a heptapeptide of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS), the hormone network that regulates blood pressure, fluid and electrolyte balance. It was characterised in 2013 and is formed from angiotensin A by ACE2, or directly from angiotensin-(1-7).

name: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone
summary: The hypothalamic hormone that tells the pituitary to make TSH; a brain-active peptide with only small, dated human studies outside diagnostics.
lead: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH, also thyroliberin; the pharmaceutical form is protirelin) is a tripeptide, pyroglutamyl-histidyl-proline amide, made mainly by neurons in the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus. It stimulates the pituitary to release thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and prolactin, and so sits at the top of the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis.
